highlights:
## Extraordinary circumstances

The overarching principle of air passenger rights guaranteed by the EU is the right 
to standard compensation if a flight is delayed or cancelled. Air passenger rights are 
based on the Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 (‘Regulation’). 
According to the Regulation, an air carrier is not required to pay standard 
compensation only if it can prove that both of the following conditions are met: 
1. The delay or cancellation of the flight was caused by extraordinary 
circumstances. 
2. The delay or cancellation could not be avoided even though the air 
carrier had taken all reasonable measures. 
If an air carrier invokes extraordinary circumstances, it must give a sufficient

question: How much compensation do I get under EU261 if my 1,500 km flight arrives 3 hours late?
reference_rule: Passengers whose flight of 1,500 kilometres or less arrives three hours or more late are entitled to compensation of EUR 250 under Article 7 of Regulation (EC) No 261/2004.
title: Air passenger rights - Consilium
highlights:
#### Right to compensation in the event of cancellation or delay

Passengers can be compensated in the event of delay or cancellation. If a flight is more than three hours late or cancelled less than 14 days before departure, a passenger could be entitled to compensation of:

- €250 for all flights of 1 500 km or less
- €400 for all intra-EU flights or flights between 1 500 km and 3 500 km
- €600 for all other flights

### Who is covered by the rules?

Passengers don't have to be EU citizens to be protected by the rules. EU air passenger rights apply to all passengers:

- flying within the EU
- departing from the EU to a non-EU country
- arriving in the EU from a non-EU country on an EU airline

highlights:
## Compensation for train delays

Thanks to the EU, you have extensive rights in this kind of situation. They apply not only when you travel from one EU country to another, but also when you travel within the EU.

If the train arrives at its destination with a delay of between 60 and 119 minutes for a one-way journey, you can claim a refund of 25% of the ticket price. If the delay is 120 minutes or more, you can claim 50% of the ticket price.

If you have bought a return ticket, the railway company will calculate the compensation on the basis of half the ticket price. For example: The ticket costs 150 euros. Depending on the length of the delay, the railway company will charge 25 or 50 percent of €75.
